reuse.why: All weekend/holiday/daily-skip behaviour is put into the existing shared applyWeekendRule, and the new range handler reuses recurConfigToRSchedule, RSchedule and applyWeekendRule rather than inventing its own adjustment.

duplication.why: The 'how far to look ahead so that skipped/moved occurrences are still covered' heuristic is written three times with different formulas (getNextDate take = 7 + 2*holidays, getUpcomingDates take = count*7 + holidays, getDatesInRange padding = 3 + 2*holidays), and getDatesInRange repeats getUpcomingDates' occurrences-then-adjust-then-filter pipeline.

placement.why: Rule logic stays in shared/schedules.ts, the handler is in server/schedules/app.ts next to get-upcoming-dates, and the rule data is threaded through parseRecurDate; only the frequency coupling inside a 'weekend rule' is slightly off-layer.

scope.why: Changes are confined to the schedule date path, tests and release notes; the schedule-template refactor into adjustOccurrence is needed because the rule can now return null.

maintainability.why: One definition of the rule is good, but the nullable return forces every caller to remember a null check and the scattered, inconsistent look-ahead constants are fragile magic numbers.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All callers (getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange, schedule-template createScheduleList) go through applyWeekendRule.

disguised_duplication.where: Look-ahead/padding heuristic reshaped in shared/schedules.ts getNextDate (WEEKEND_SKIP_LOOKAHEAD), server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates (count*7) and getDatesInRange (WEEKEND_ADJUST_PADDING_DAYS) instead of one helper.

abstraction_drift.where: shared/schedules.ts applyWeekendRule: WeekendRule gains frequency and holidays, plus a frequency==='daily' return-null branch that changes the return type to Date | null for all callers; no caller bypasses it.
